dict.string: nightjar-hack listens for Bluetooth devices around you and logs what it hears. If you use the Send tab, it can also advertise a payload you type and write to devices you choose. Listening never connects to anything.
nightjar-hack sends payloads to, and receives payloads from, devices on your local network — only to addresses you type, and only while the app is open.

nightjar-hack's compass uses your heading and direction of travel to point you toward a Bluetooth device its ear is hearing, while you walk to it. Your location is never stored and never leaves the phone.

nightjar-hack uses the camera to receive Blink transmissions — messages another of your devices shows as a looping sequence of QR frames — only while you hold the Blink receiver open in the Knocktalk tab. Frames are decoded in the moment; no photos or video are taken or stored.
nightjar-hack reads a tag you hold to the phone when you use the Coin — a physical key you claim in the EMCON tab. The tag is only read at the moment you tap, and only a hash of it is kept.

nightjar-hack listens for Chirp transmissions — short messages another of your devices sends as audible tones — only while you hold the Chirp listener open in the Knocktalk tab. Nothing is recorded or stored; tones are decoded in the moment and forgotten.

nightjar-hack reads the readings your Apple Watch already collects — heart rate, blood oxygen, breath, wrist temperature, and sleep — to show the state of the operator beside the state of the house. It only reads; nothing is written to your health data, and nothing leaves this phone.
